name: Opus Value
strategy: Contrarian value in capitulated quality: managed care tilted toward the cheapest name (Cigna), de-rated cash-flow software and search (Adobe, Alphabet) bought into the AI-regulation selloff, a reduced integrated-energy hedge plus physical gold against a still-live Gulf supply risk, and 25% cash.
reassessment_note: Researched via Yahoo Finance price/quote/news feeds and articles (web search returned mostly stale April-2026 coverage). Three things changed. (1) Oil's war premium is deflating: Dated Brent's premium over futures collapsed from ~$30 to ~$3.70, Gulf producers lifted October exports ~10% and Aramco says it will maximize output, Goldman pegs ~$27/bbl of price as war premium; Brent fell ~16% in five days to ~$98 and XOM/CVX are off ~11% from 10-30. Tanker attacks continue, so I keep a hedge but cut energy from 23% to 15%. (2) Democrats won both chambers on 11-03; Warren is targeting UnitedHealth with the Break Up Big Medicine Act, but it needs GOP votes and faces a veto, so I trim UNH (Optum margin still 2.6% vs 6-8% target) and rotate into Cigna, which just raised 2026 EPS guidance and trades at 8.8x forward. (3) The 11-05 crash (S&P -4.4%, Nasdaq -5.5%) was an AI-regulation scare; it pushed quality cash-flow names to capitulation multiples (ADBE 8.7x forward with a rare Citi Sell, GOOGL 18x forward and 30% off its high), which is exactly this book's mandate. ETH is dropped: it was a leftover from the retired staples-and-crypto hedge, sits -17.6% and in downtrend. ACN's take-profit cash is partly redeployed; 25% cash stays given VIX ~28.

positions.thesis: Largest leg because it is the cheapest managed-care name with the best fundamental momentum: Q3 beat with raised full-year 2026 EPS outlook and a reset that clears the 2027 base, at 8.8x forward earnings versus UNH ~17x and ELV ~14x. Less exposed to the Medicare Advantage/Optum vertical-integration attack than UNH. Upsized from 14% to 18%.

Margin-recovery thesis intact (EPS seen rising from ~$16 in 2025 toward ~$23 in 2027, 18x forward below its 19x five-year average, ETFs and institutions buying), but trimmed from 16% to 14% because a Democratic Congress makes Warren's break-up rhetoric louder and Optum Health margins are still far below target; the 2027 outlook before year-end is the next catalyst.

The inflation-shock and policy hedge that is working: gold had its best day since August after the midterms and is back above $4,000 on a weaker-dollar narrative and record central-bank buying, while GLD still sits 27% below its 52-week high. Nudged from 11% to 12% as energy is cut, so the hedge sleeve shifts toward the asset not dependent on the war premium.

Kept as the core of the energy hedge because Hormuz flows are still below pre-war levels and tankers are still being hit, but cut from 14% to 10% since physical premiums have collapsed and Goldman's base case has prices falling below the forward curve as the ~$27 war premium fades. At ~13x forward on elevated oil it is fair, not cheap, so it is a hedge position, not a value bet.

Classic capitulated quality: down ~29% YTD, 8.7x forward earnings, and Citi just issued a rare Sell, the kind of sentiment extreme this book buys. The AI-disruption fear is priced at a multiple that implies terminal decline, while Adobe still prints heavy free cash flow and buys back stock. Upsized from 7% to 9%, with a wide 18% stop to survive the volatility.

New leg: Alphabet is ~30% below its 52-week high and below its 200-day average after the AI and regulation selloff, at ~18x forward and ~15x trailing for a net-cash, cash-flow machine. Sized small at 7% because post-election AI and data-center regulation risk is real and directly targets it; this is an entry into capitulation, not a momentum chase.

Small secondary energy hedge (cut from 9% to 5%), kept for its 3.35% dividend, ~12.9x forward multiple and the tail risk of renewed Gulf disruption; sized down for the same war-premium-deflation reason as XOM.
